checks: A finite concave radius has finite positive one-sided limits at the two endpoints. Replacing endpoint values preserves all the records, since any nonzero finite slope meets each axial endpoint in a point of zero line measure and s=0 stays in the interior. The supporting affine majorant still holds at the new endpoints.

The inverse-projective expression for the radius is a concave perspective on the positive denominator interval. It attains its maximum at zero by the affine majorant. Along either ray it is nonincreasing, so for each fixed q the density e_s(q) is bounded and nonincreasing until it leaves support. The m=1 power is used only on the positive support.

Changing to z′ and then z′=s q produces C=∫(1−b_0 s q)^−d e_s and M=∫s q(1−b_0 s q)^−d−1 e_s. The raw coarea Jacobian contributes two powers and the radius contributes m−1, totaling d. At a fixed slope the endpoint and supporting equality exceptions affect at most finitely many q, using strict monotonicity of z/r(z) on the interior.

The weight denominator is uniformly positive on the compact transformed axial range, including every deletion point of e_s. The smooth extension only defines the weight away from where it is used. The BV product rule gives the absolutely continuous contribution d b_0 M(s) ds/s and the negative weighted Stieltjes loss. Uniform density and variation bounds justify integrating over q. The same-batch cap derivative cancels the absolutely continuous term exactly.

The section formula gives continuity for s>0. As s tends to zero the x-parameterized section tends to the own section by bounded convergence, and the cap integral tends to P(0). As s tends to infinity the coarea is O(1/s) and the clipped axial cap fraction tends to one half. Thus the negative measure derivative gives all interval and total-mass identities, including nonnegativity from the zero tail limit.

Compared 5b3b585d1663ccd0 §7, (10)–(14). As an independent exact arithmetic calibration for r(z)=1+z/2 on [−1,1], the computed F-values at slopes 1/3, 2/3, 1, 2 and 4 are respectively 5/4, 5/4, 7/8, 1/2 and 1/4, including the two distinct axial deletion transitions.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use the same finite positive concave profile and interval-layer definition. Its exact formula gives local absolute continuity of P and dP=−M(s) ds/s on positive slopes, with the same raw vertical moment. The coarea formula also gives continuity at positive s because wR is integrable.

overlap.comparison: Provides raw coarea in a reciprocal-radius coordinate with stronger profile regularity. It does not prove the monotonic combination using an affine-majorant chart or the loss measure.
Its nonnegative support defect is a single-section integral after centering. It is not a Stieltjes loss identity along varying slopes.

readability: The right-limit representatives change the integrand only on a q-null set at each fixed slope. The weight is read on the support of the corresponding Stieltjes measure, where no denominator pole occurs.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The cap derivative cancels the absolutely continuous weight derivative in coarea, leaving the nonnegative Stieltjes measure of support and density losses.
